because the findings were foundations-level and page-level fixes applied

whose findings drove the fixes; recording five rounds of one view would make
the gate arithmetic meaningless. All six reviewers of round 5 read ONE frozen
capture, sha256

applied AFTER the round and the tree re-exported and re-captured, which is what a
resolution IS. Each one names the source change, and several carry a measurement
taken on the rebuilt page. Rounds 1-4 are not recorded; recording five rounds of
What the loop measured, rather than asserted:
round 1  6/6 reviewers led with the same P1 — the product's entire call to
action rendered as the weakest control on the page. The primary
button measured 1.04:1 before and 6.29:1 after.
round 2  that P1 is gone from all six. New: the section-heading level
collides with the hero identifier; one grey does four jobs.
round 3  L2 measures the rhythm and reports 'one scale, correct proximity',
and that 'the classic label/value misalignment this view is warned
about did not happen'. L1 calls the type scale 'sound'.
round 4  the last foundations P1 clears. Remaining findings are P2/P3.
round 5  RECORDED BELOW. ZERO P1s carry a rubric criterion — every P1 is a
presence failure. L3 independently measured every text-on-surface
pair and reported no contrast failures anywhere.
Every round-5 P1 is a PRESENCE failure — age, a copy affordance, the value /
nonce / type rows, the receipt payload, the 'supply an ABI' action. That is
content nobody has built. All fifteen are recorded verbatim, none is
resolved, and the FULL gate holds every one against this page (G1 and G3 both
fail). They are VD.4's. The foundations gate excludes them by construction —
a finding with no rubric criterion is a missing element, and a missing
element is content — and prints the whole excluded set on every run rather
than dropping it.

G4 and G5 are EMPTY and stay empty. Both require a named human — brief §11
says so of G5 in as many words ('Not an agent'), and gate.mjs enforces `by`
and `date` on both. No agent may create them. Writing a plausible name into
either field would be the one edit that defeats the gate, so the foundations
round reports FAILED on exactly those two conditions and on nothing else.
That is the honest ceiling of an agent-run round, and it is where VD.2 stops.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash

findings.location: hero, between the H1 hash line and the trace card
findings.finding: The hero carries only the truncated hash, a 'Succeeded' pill and the full hash string. Age is absent from the page entirely, the finality badge appears only as a 'Pending' row inside the Overview grid rather than in the hero, and the full hash at y approx 288 has no copy affordance of any kind.

findings.location: Overview grid, rows BLOCK through COST · MANA
findings.finding: The grid has six rows: BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST · MANA. Value, nonce and transaction type are absent as labelled rows, and COST · MANA is a resource limit/usage pair, not the required fee breakdown, so no fee figure appears anywhere on the page.

findings.location: Decoded input section, note box below the SELECTOR / RAW table
findings.finding: The unknown-selector path shows raw bytes plus the sentence 'Supplying an ABI decodes them.' set as ordinary body prose. There is no 'supply an ABI' action - no button, no link, no distinguishing type treatment - so the required affordance is present only as a description of one.

findings.location: hero, H1 hash line and the full-hash line 30px below it
findings.finding: The H1 truncates the hash to 10+8 characters at ~32px, and the complete 66-character hash is then set immediately beneath it at ~14px. The visually dominant instance is the incomplete one and the truncation buys nothing. The breadcrumb above truncates the same hash again at 6+4, so one identifier appears at three different lengths inside 130 vertical pixels with no single truncation rule.

findings.location: hero, 'Succeeded' badge to the right of the H1
findings.finding: The status badge is the smallest type in the hero at roughly 11px, set beside a ~32px H1. Status is the second most important fact on a transaction page and on a product whose reason to exist is reverted transactions; at this weight the hierarchy says the hash matters and the outcome is an annotation.

findings.location: Overview grid, COST · MANA value cell
findings.finding: '42000 / 100000 mana(FeeJuice)' sets the two figures, the unit and the token name at one monospace size, weight and colour, so the unit reads as more identifier. The digits carry no thousands grouping, and there is no space before '(FeeJuice)'. The unit and token should drop to the secondary text level so the numbers are the scannable part.

findings.location: hero, full-hash line at y approx 288
findings.finding: The full hash is set at the same size, weight, colour and face as a value cell in the Overview grid and carries no label. Typographically it reads as an orphaned table value that lost its row rather than as the page's canonical identifier.

findings.location: H1 versus the six section headings (Overview, Decoded input, Events, Internal calls, State changes, Raw (chain-native))
findings.finding: The H1 is monospace while every section heading is the proportional sans. The page's top heading level therefore does not sit on the same scale as its second level, and the six section headings are the only true heading rung the eye can navigate by.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section, JSON block
findings.finding: The JSON is set at roughly 13px on a ~1.55 line-height, barely denser than the 14px body around it. This is the one product-register element on a web-register page and the density difference should look chosen; at present it reads as the same rhythm on a grey surface.

findings.location: 'Raw (chain-native)' section heading
findings.finding: The parenthetical qualifier is set at the same size and weight as the heading noun, so 'chain-native' competes with 'Raw' for the scanning eye. Every other section heading is a single word or short phrase, making this one visually the longest and heaviest.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash
Decoded input: 'supply an ABI' action for the unknown selector

findings.location: hero, y163-296 (breadcrumb to full hash line)
findings.finding: The hero shows status ('Succeeded' badge at x843-1015) and the full hash (y284, x505-904) but omits three required items: the age, the finality badge, and any copy affordance beside the full hash. Finality is present only as a 'Pending' row inside the Overview grid at y874-915, which is not the hero.

findings.location: Overview grid (y791-1039), Decoded input note (y1325-1402), Raw block (y2351-2522)
findings.finding: Required data is absent. The Overview grid has only six rows (Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost · Mana) - no value, no nonce, no transaction type, no fee breakdown. Decoded input states 'Supplying an ABI decodes them' as prose with no action control. The Raw block contains a single 5-line transaction object and no receipt payload, and the two payloads are not labelled or distinguished.

findings.location: all six section headings (Overview y742, Decoded input y1169, Events y1534, Internal calls y1790, State changes y2046, Raw y2301)
findings.finding: Every section heading is equidistant between the divider above it and the content below it: rule-to-heading is 28-30px and heading-to-content is 25-30px at all six sections (e.g. rule y712 -> 'Overview' y742 = 29px; heading bottom y760 -> table top y791 = 30px). No heading is bound by proximity to the block it labels, so across eight sections in one scroll the page reads as an evenly spaced strip of rules and items rather than six titled sections.

findings.location: right edge of the content column, whole page
findings.finding: Two container widths alternate down the right edge. Section rules, the Overview table, the Decoded-input table and the Raw block all end at x=1415 (911px wide); the trace card and all four notice boxes end at x=1203 (699px wide). The step repeats five times, and inside a single section - Decoded input - the table ending at 1415 sits 23px above a note ending at 1203, a 212px jog within one section.

findings.location: section aprons, y1503-2171 (Events, Internal calls, State changes)
findings.finding: The spacing apron is identical regardless of what the section holds: 100-101px above each rule, ~29px rule-to-heading, ~28px heading-to-content, for a 249px Overview table and for a 76-77px one-sentence notice alike. Events, Internal calls and State changes therefore consume 668px of vertical scroll to deliver three single sentences. The amount of space is not readable as a decision.

findings.location: trace card, hairline divider at y544
findings.finding: The divider inside the trace card runs x529-1138 while the card's content box runs x529-1178 (border 504-1203, padding 25px, confirmed by the Generate trace button's left edge at x529). It is inset 25px on the left and 65px on the right, so the only rule inside the page's most prominent card is visibly asymmetric.

findings.location: Overview table (x504-1415) and Decoded-input table (x504-1415)
findings.finding: Both tables are stretched to the column rather than sized to their data. The Overview table's longest value ends at x=1042, leaving a 373px dead column to the right of every row; the Decoded-input table's longest value ends at x=772, leaving 643px. At 1920 this is the wide viewport being consumed rather than used.

findings.location: boundary between the trace card (bottom border y620) and the first section rule (y712)
findings.finding: That gap is 92px, where every other section boundary measures 100-101px (y1039->1139, y1402->1503, y1658->1759, y1915->2016, y2171->2272). The one boundary that separates the hero from the body is the tightest on the page, by 9px.

findings.location: Overview grid, value column, rows Canonical (y832-874) and Finality (y874-915)
findings.finding: The two status badges have their box left edge at x=680 while every text value in the same column begins at x=689/690. The badge label is optically aligned but the badge box overhangs, so the value column's visible left edge ripples by 9px twice down six rows.

missing: hero: copy affordance on the full hash
raw section: the receipt payload, and labelling distinguishing transaction from receipt
decoded input: the 'supply an ABI' action (prose only, no control)

findings.location: hero, the H1 hash and the full hash line beneath it (y≈240–290)
findings.finding: No age and no finality badge appear in the hero — finality is only present as a 'Pending' row in the Overview grid — and neither the truncated H1 nor the full hash carries any copy affordance.

findings.location: Overview grid
findings.finding: The grid has six rows (Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost · Mana). Value, nonce and transaction type are absent entirely.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section
findings.finding: The block contains only a five-line transaction-shaped object (aztec.kind, aztec.contract). The receipt payload is absent and the two payloads are neither labelled nor distinguishable, so 'transaction and receipt JSON verbatim' is not satisfied.

findings.location: Decoded input section, note panel below the selector/raw rows
findings.finding: The unknown-selector path renders the sentence 'Supplying an ABI decodes them.' but no 'supply an ABI' control — the specified action exists only as prose.

findings.location: trace card (hero, y≈340–615) vs Overview table vs Raw block
findings.finding: Three unrelated containment idioms on one page: the trace card has no border and is bounded only by a diffuse shadow; the Overview table and the Events/Internal-calls/State-changes panels use a ~#A2A2A2 1px hairline; the Raw block is a bare #ECECEB fill. There is no surface/elevation ladder, and the card carrying the primary action is the least-defined surface on the page.

findings.location: 'Succeeded' badge (hero) and 'Canonical: Yes' badge (Overview row 2) vs 'On demand' badge (trace card)
findings.finding: The page's single green role (#DCFCE7 / #166534) carries two different meanings — execution status and a boolean registry fact — while the trace-availability badge, the state the whole page turns on, is the only badge with no hue at all: a neutral dark dot on white with a hairline. Colour weight is allocated inversely to consequence.

findings.location: breadcrumb, 'TRANSACTION' eyebrow, Overview label column, the three explanation panels, footer
findings.finding: The text-emphasis ladder is compressed to #101010 / #242424 / #484848 / #565656. #484848 alone carries breadcrumb, eyebrow, grid labels, all explanatory prose and the footer, and #565656 is only 1.24:1 from it, so the last two levels are indistinguishable and colour does almost no hierarchy work.

findings.location: section rules between Overview / Decoded input / Events / Internal calls / State changes / Raw, and the header separator
findings.finding: Structural rules are #C8C8C8 on white — 1.86:1, below the 3:1 non-text floor — and the panel hairlines are ~2.6:1, so the page's containment is carried entirely by boundaries that are near-invisible on a bright display.

findings.location: whole page palette
findings.finding: The palette is stock framework values — pure neutral greys plus indigo-600 (#4F46E5) and green-100/800 — and the accent appears only twice (Generate trace fill, link colour). The theme reads as defaults not yet replaced rather than a designed light palette with an identity.

missing: hero: copy affordance on the full hash
hero: finality badge (Finality appears only as a grid row, not in the hero)
overview grid: fee breakdown (only a cost/limit usage row is shown)
decoded input: 'supply an ABI' action for the unknown selector
raw section: the chain-native receipt JSON

findings.location: hero (y≈240–290), overview grid (six rows, y≈795–1037), decoded-input section, raw section
findings.finding: Required facts are absent: the hero shows the full hash with no copy affordance and carries no age and no finality badge; the overview grid has only BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET and COST·MANA — no value, nonce, transaction type or fee breakdown; the decoded-input section states 'Supplying an ABI decodes them' in prose but offers no 'supply an ABI' control; the raw section shows one four-key transaction object and no receipt payload.

findings.location: whole page — content column spans x≈500–1415 of a 1920 px viewport
findings.finding: The wide viewport buys the page nothing. A single ~915 px column is used at every viewport, so roughly 1000 px of horizontal space is unused while the page runs to 2785 px vertically for about fifteen facts. The overview grid's value column is ~730 px wide to hold a 42-character address and a three-character 'Yes' badge; the decoded-input grid's value column holds '0x1a2b3c4d' and '0x' in the same 730 px. A two-column overview grid, or sections paired side by side, would put the whole factual payload in one screen.

findings.location: section separators between Overview, Decoded input, Events, Internal calls, State changes and Raw (rules at y≈707, 1135, 1504, 1752, 2010, 2256)
findings.finding: Section spacing is uniform regardless of section weight: each section ends ~100 px above its following rule and rules sit ~180–430 px apart whether the section holds a six-row table or a single sentence. Events, Internal calls and State changes are three near-identical one-sentence notices, each in a 700×~75 px card, spread across ~750 px of scroll — three facts for two-thirds of a screen. The gaps do not encode grouping, so the page reads as long rather than as structured.

findings.location: trace card (y≈348–608) and the Events / Internal calls / State changes notice cards versus the overview grid, decoded-input grid and raw block
findings.finding: Two content widths coexist in one scroll: the notice and trace cards end at x≈1195 while the grids, the raw block and the section rules run to x≈1405–1415. The 210 px difference leaves a ragged right edge on five of the eight sections and gives the eye no single right margin to scan against.

findings.location: decoded-input grid, RAW row (y≈1265)
findings.finding: The RAW row's value is the two characters '0x' — an empty calldata payload rendered as a full-height grid row. At realistic volume this section will hold a long hex string in the same cell, so this capture does not exercise the section's density case at all; a reviewer cannot judge the wrapping strategy from it.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash
Overview grid: fee breakdown (fee amount, not only mana cost/limit)

findings.location: hero, beside the truncated hash and the full hash line below it
findings.finding: The hero carries only a 'Succeeded' chip. Age is absent from the hero and from the entire page, the finality badge appears only as a row inside the Overview grid, and the full hash on the second line has no copy affordance.

findings.location: Overview grid
findings.finding: The grid has six rows (Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost·Mana). Value, nonce and transaction type are absent, and there is no fee amount — only a mana cost/limit pair, which is the resource-usage requirement, not the fee breakdown.

findings.location: Decoded input section, notice panel below the Selector/Raw rows
findings.finding: For an unknown selector the spec requires raw bytes AND a 'supply an ABI' action. Only the sentence 'Supplying an ABI decodes them.' is present; there is no control to supply one, so the page describes an affordance it does not offer.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section
findings.finding: The block contains one four-line transaction object under an 'aztec' key. The receipt payload is absent and neither payload is labelled, so the section cannot be read as 'transaction and receipt, verbatim'.

findings.location: trace card (hero) versus the notice panels in Events, Internal calls and State changes
findings.finding: The page's primary action sits inside a bordered rounded panel that is the same shared primitive as the three 'nothing here yet' notices below it. The container that carries the product's most important control is visually indistinguishable from the container that carries its absences.

findings.location: trace card line 'Internal calls and state changes come from the execution trace.' versus the Internal calls and State changes panels
findings.finding: One fact, two vocabularies: the trace card says data 'comes from' the execution trace while both section panels say it is 'read from' it. The specified sentence is a shared primitive and its two paraphrases below make the page read as written by two hands.

findings.location: Events notice panel, and the trace card body copy
findings.finding: Internal architecture leaks into visitor-facing copy: 'once this chain's receipts are published to the data plane this page reads' (Events) and 'runs it again under the recorder' (trace card). Both name implementation surfaces a visitor has no model for, in a register that is otherwise plain-spoken.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section, the grey preformatted block
findings.finding: The one product-register element on the page is rendered as plain near-black monospace on a flat grey fill with no CodeTracer editor tokens, no panel header and no copy control. The product's single sanctioned register crossing is not made here, so the page's only code reads as an inert slab rather than as CodeTracer.

findings.location: trace card, primary button label 'Generate trace'
findings.finding: The primary action is labelled with a different verb from the product's signature 'Debug' used everywhere a transaction appears. The on-demand state justifies a distinct label, but nothing on the page ties 'Generate trace' back to debugging, so the page's strongest control does not read as the product's one promise.

findings.location: trace card body copy, clause 'it takes a moment, it needs an account'
findings.finding: Three unlike facts — a duration, an account requirement and a privacy claim — are strung into one sentence at equal weight, so the only one with a consequence for the visitor is the least prominent. 'A moment' is also the page's one unquantified quantity.

findings.location: footer, second line
findings.finding: 'Rendered from demo data (blocktracer-demo-gen)' sets the right honest tone but exposes an internal package name in monospace on a public surface; the human-readable half of the sentence already carries the meaning.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash
Hero: finality badge (rendered in the Overview grid instead)
Raw section: the chain-native receipt JSON (only a single unlabelled transaction object is shown)

findings.location: Overview section, the six-row fact grid below the trace card (y approx 790-1030)
findings.finding: The Overview grid carries six rows where Page-Descriptions 7.2 names eight facts: value, fee breakdown, nonce and transaction type are all absent, and their place is taken by CANONICAL and FINALITY badge rows (FINALITY being a hero requirement demoted into the grid). The omission is not a data limit - the raw block further down the page exposes "kind": "public-avm-call", so the transaction type is available and simply was never given a labelled row. The narrow 130px label column against an ~800px value column leaves every row two-thirds empty, confirming visually that the grid was populated from whatever the adapter exposed rather than from the specified fact set.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane (x 1150–1432), FEE PAYER row y 325–372 and TARGET row y 400–447
findings.finding: The 42-character addresses hard-wrap into three right-aligned monospace lines whose last line holds two characters — '32' for FEE PAYER, '4c' for TARGET. A right-aligned three-line block with a two-glyph tail reads as three separate values, and the wrap points (21/19/2) fall mid-byte so no fragment is a meaningful boundary. The same wrap-to-orphan pattern recurs in the STATE pane's `masses` row (y 675–710), where '14]' sits alone on the second line.

findings.location: identity bar hash (x 93, y 31) vs TRANSACTION pane hash (x 1232, y 162); call trace rows 4 and 7 (y 343, y 418); editor line 26 (y 320)
findings.finding: Five overflow strategies coexist on one screen with no rule connecting them: middle-ellipsis at 6+4 in the identity bar (0xb63616…6359); middle-ellipsis at 8+8 for the SAME hash in the transaction pane (0xb636167a…66d46359); end-ellipsis on call-trace symbols and paths; hard wrap in the transaction pane; and a soft right-edge fade on source lines. The identical hash truncated to two different lengths 1 050 px apart is the clearest case — a reader cannot tell at a glance that they are the same value.

findings.location: DEBUG CONTROLS readout, y 172, x 475–1130; against CALL TRACE opcode column, x 1090–1135
findings.finding: The trace length is rendered three times in two formats. The controls line carries it twice on one line and in two faces — 'Step 128 of 1315' in the UI sans, then '128 / 1315' in monospace 40 px later — while the call trace renders the same 1315 as '1,315' with a thousands separator. The STATE pane then uses ungrouped 10000 / 2000 / 1000, and COST · MANA uses ungrouped '88000 / 200000'. Program values arguably should stay verbatim, but the step counter and the opcode counts are UI figures and must pick one grouping rule.

findings.location: CALL TRACE pane, title at y 216 and column header row at y 241
findings.finding: Two hierarchy levels are set identically: 'CALL TRACE' (pane title) and 'FRAME' (column header) are both ~11 px letterspaced caps in near-identical grey, 25 px apart and separated only by a hairline, so the header row reads as a second pane title. Within that same header row the casing is mixed — 'FRAME' all-caps against 'ACIR opcodes' in mixed case — so the two column labels do not read as a pair.

findings.location: EDITOR pane, annotation at y 273–293, directly above source line 26
findings.finding: The explanatory note 'Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window.' is set in the same monospace face, the same size and near-identical colour as the source beneath it. The only thing distinguishing prose from program text is the absent line number, so the eye lands on two lines of UI copy before it reaches the code and the current position. An annotation needs its own level — smaller, or the UI sans, or a clearly demoted colour.

findings.location: EDITOR source rows (22 px pitch), CALL TRACE rows and STATE rows (both ~25 px pitch)
findings.finding: Leading runs 1.7× in the source pane and ~1.9× in the call-trace and state panes at a 13 px monospace. That is explorer-register rhythm inside the product register: the call trace shows seven frames in a 210 px body where ~1.45 leading would show ten, and the editor shows 26 lines where it would show ~30. The fix adds information rather than removing it, which is the test the debugger rubric sets.

findings.location: identity bar, x 24–202, y 31
findings.finding: '← aztec' is the only link-styled element in the bar (blue, sans); the truncated hash 40 px to its right is near-black monospace with no underline, no colour and no weight change. Typographically nothing in the identity bar signals the route back to the transaction detail page — the one navigable-looking element points at the chain. The hash is the strongest type on the bar and should carry the affordance.

findings.location: EDITOR pane text column, right edge x ≈ 680; lines 26, 40, 41, 42, 43, 48, 49
findings.finding: The source measure is ~66 monospace columns, and 7 of the 26 visible lines fade out mid-token — including line 26, the call whose result the current line 32 consumes, and the signature on line 40. The fade is a deliberate treatment rather than a clip, but at this measure it is doing real work on a quarter of the visible source in a file written to ~90 columns.

findings.location: STATE pane, type column at x 1095–1138
findings.finding: A categorical text column ('Field', '[Field; 8]', 'u32') is right-aligned, so its left edge ripples against an otherwise clean value column. Alignment should follow data type: the numeric column right, the type labels left.

findings.location: EDITOR tab strip, y 242, x 22–412
findings.finding: The four tabs (Nargo.toml, Prover.toml, src/main.nr, src/shield.nr) are identical in face, size, weight and very nearly in colour; the active file is carried by a 1 px underline alone. One weight or colour step would let the active file be read without hunting for the rule.

findings.location: phase chips in the banner, y 78–102, x 650–1325
findings.finding: 'FETCHING THE ENGINE AND THE TRACE' and 'POSITIONING AT THE REQUESTED STEP' are 30+ character all-caps letterspaced strings at ~11 px. All-caps removes word shape at exactly the length where it matters most, and these chips are the element a waiting visitor is meant to read fastest. Sentence case at the same size would be quicker to parse and would still read as a status chip.

findings.location: EDITOR pane (x 4–686) versus TRANSACTION pane (x 1149–1435) and CALL TRACE pane (y 205–533)
findings.finding: The column split starves the flagship pane and pads the others. The editor is 683 px wide and truncates lines 26, 40, 41, 42, 43, 48 and 49 at x~667 behind a uniform 19 px opaque fade band (x 667–685, constant #EEEEED for the pane's full height, no scrollbar thumb anywhere in 660 rows), while the TRANSACTION pane runs empty for 251 px (y 641–891, a third of its height) and the CALL TRACE pane runs empty for 81 px (y 451–531). The same fade also dims the final word of the wrapped, non-truncated info line at y 272, so undamaged prose reads as disabled.

findings.location: gutter between CALL TRACE (bottom border y 533) and STATE (top border y 566)
findings.finding: This gutter is 32 px while every other seam on the page is 4–6 px: banner-to-DEBUG-CONTROLS is 4 px (y 116–119), DEBUG-CONTROLS-to-EDITOR is 6 px (y 199–204), and both column gutters are 4 px (x 687–690 and x 1145–1148). One gutter at 8x the others is not one spacing scale, and it costs 32 px of vertical room in a viewport where the editor is already slicing its last line.

findings.location: left edge of the page, identity bar (y 0–62) and banner (y 64–115) against the pane grid (y 120 down)
findings.finding: Two competing page gutters. The identity bar and the loading banner are full-bleed with 24 px inner padding ('←' at x 25, banner prose at x 24, 'Download trace' right edge at x 1415, i.e. 24 px from the viewport edge). The pane grid sits on a 4 px margin (pane borders at x 4 and x 1435) with 9–10 px header insets, so 'DEBUG CONTROLS' starts at x 13 and 'EDITOR' at x 14. Nothing in the top 200 px of the page shares a left edge: 25, 24, 13, 17 (first stepping button box at x 17).

findings.location: DEBUG CONTROLS pane, stepping button row (x 17–269, y 159–188)
findings.finding: Measured at y 173 the eight buttons are 29, 29, 27, 26, 32, 32, 32, 32 px wide — four different control sizes in one row, because each box is sized to its glyph rather than to a fixed control size. All seven inter-button gaps are an identical 2 px, so the four semantic pairs (reverse/forward, step-in/step-out, line-back/line-forward, start/end) get no proximity grouping at all; the controls read as one undifferentiated run of eight and the reverse control is not visually paired with its forward twin.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane value column, FEE PAYER (y 313–384) and TARGET (y 385–456) against the identity hash at y 150–175
findings.finding: Two overflow strategies for the same kind of value, 200 px apart in one pane. The identity hash at the top is middle-truncated ('0xb636167a…66d46359', right edge x 1389), while FEE PAYER and TARGET hard-wrap in full onto three right-aligned lines each, leaving two-character orphans ('32' and '4c') alone on the last line. The consequence is row rhythm: those two rows are 69 px tall against 31 px for BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY, so the pane's grid reads as three unrelated blocks rather than one fact table.

findings.location: CALL TRACE pane, frame rows y 255–431
findings.finding: The depth ladder is uneven. Frame-name left edges are x 702 (main, d0), 724 (d1), 740 (d2), 756 (d3): the first step is 22 px and every later step is 16 px, so d0-to-d1 and d1-to-d2 do not look like the same move. A vertical guide rule is drawn only at depth 1 (x 706); depths 2 and 3 are expressed by indentation alone, which is what B6 asks to avoid.

findings.location: STATE pane, below the 'i / 2 / u32' row (y 864–892)
findings.finding: A row separator is drawn at y 863 under the last value row, leaving a 29 px ruled but empty stub — exactly one row height — between it and the pane's bottom border at y 893. It reads as a blank table row rather than as the end of the table.

findings.location: STATE / EVENT LOG tab strip, active-tab underline at y 589–590
findings.finding: The underline spans x 692–744, starting 1 px from the pane's inner left edge, while the 'STATE' label it underlines starts at x 700. The rule is offset 8 px to the left of the word it belongs to and sits flush against the pane border, so it reads as a pane edge decoration rather than as the tab's selected state.

findings.location: loading banner phase chips (y 77–101) against the identity bar controls (y 18–46)
findings.finding: Two adjacent full-bleed bands with right edges 92 px apart: the third chip 'POSITIONING AT THE REQUESTED STEP' ends at x 1323 while 'Download trace' directly above it ends at x 1415, and the pane grid below ends at x 1435. The chips are left-flowing after the prose rather than right-aligned to the banner's own 24 px padding, leaving a 92 px ragged notch in the page's right edge at the top of the view. (The three chips are internally consistent — 12 px gaps at x 903–916 and 1058–1071.)

findings.location: EDITOR pane, header / tab strip / info line (y 205–300)
findings.finding: Three left edges inside 95 px of vertical space: the 'EDITOR' header label at x 14, the first file tab 'Nargo.toml' at x 22, and the 'Showing from line 26 —' info line at x 13. The tab strip is inset 8–9 px further than the two rules above and below it, so the pane's left rail visibly steps in and back out.

findings.location: EDITOR pane bottom edge (y ~893)
findings.finding: The code viewport's height is not a multiple of the 23 px line height, so line 51 is sliced roughly in half by the pane's bottom border — the digits '51' and the brace are cut mid-glyph. It reads as a rendering accident rather than as a scroll position, and it is the more conspicuous because the STATE pane immediately to its right ends on a full empty row and the TRANSACTION pane ends on 251 px of white.

findings.location: STATE pane, 'masses' row (y 671–712)
findings.finding: The array value wraps, making this row 42 px tall against the uniform 25 px of every other row in the table, so the column's scanning rhythm breaks at one point. The '[Field; 8]' type stays on the first line at the x 1134 type rail while the value's continuation '14]' hangs alone on the second line, leaving the type cell looking vertically detached from the bottom half of its own row.

findings.location: EDITOR pane, code body x 70–683, y 305–890 (lines 26–51)
findings.finding: The source has no syntax highlighting whatsoever. Keywords (let, mut, if, else, fn, as), types (Field, u32), numerals (100, 0, 1) and the line-41 comment '// shields regain a percentage of the maxium capacity' all render at one flat #242424. A saturation scan of the whole code body finds 60 chromatic pixels, every one of them indigo bleed from the line-32 rail. Design-System §7 and brief §3 make the CodeTracer editor palette the one sanctioned register crossing; here there is no editor palette to cross with. The clearest cost is that a comment is indistinguishable from executable code.

findings.location: whole page — indigo #4F46E5 at: '← aztec' (x 24–76, y 31), 'Sort by cost' (x 1063, y 443), '101:0' (x 1381, y 235), line-32 rail and line number (x 5–6, y 446–469), selected call-trace rail and frame name (x 692–693, y 381–405), changed-value rails and values '9000' / '2000' (x 692–693; y 623–646, y 790–813)
findings.finding: One accent hue carries six distinct meanings: navigation link, action link, active loading phase, current position, row selection, and changed-since-last-step. The 2 px indigo left rail specifically means 'current line' in the editor, 'selected frame' in the call trace and 'value changed' in the state pane — three different things, one identical token. The only secondary differentiator is an underline, and it is applied to two of the three links ('Sort by cost', '101:0') but not to '← aztec'. In a debugger the current-position role and the diff role are the two that must never be confusable, and here they are the same colour at the same width in adjacent panes.

findings.location: DEBUG CONTROLS pane, the eight stepping buttons at x 18–267, y 159–187
findings.finding: Glyph #727272 on face #DDDDDD measures 3.54:1, and the face against the white pane behind it measures 1.36:1. That is the lowest contrast pair on the page by a wide margin — every other text-on-surface pair I measured lands between 6.29:1 and 19:1 — and it lands on the controls this product's premise depends on. If the grey is the disabled state (the banner says stepping has not started), disabled is not legible AS a state: there is no enabled control anywhere on screen to read it against, so the cluster reads as low-quality rather than as deliberately inactive.

findings.location: EDITOR pane header (y 205–229) against its code body (y 260–890), compared with the CALL TRACE / STATE / TRANSACTION pane headers
findings.finding: The editor's header bar and its code body are both #F3F3F3, so the pane header separates from its own content only by a #C8C8C8 hairline. Every other pane puts an #F3F3F3 header over a #FFFFFF body, so the surface step exists in three panes and is missing in the one that most needs it. #F3F3F3 is simultaneously the phase banner (y 63–120), all five pane headers, the editor tab strip, the editor code surface, and the neutral badge fill — one tone doing five structurally unrelated jobs, which is why the pane grid reads as flat.

findings.location: page-wide palette — neutrals #FFFFFF, #F3F3F3, #ECECEB, #DDDDDD, #C8C8C8, #A2A2A2, #242424; accents indigo-100/500/600, orange-100/800 ('Partial'), green-100/800 ('Trace ready')
findings.finding: The theme reads as inherited rather than designed for this register. Every neutral is fully desaturated stock grey and every accent is a default framework tint pair; there is no editor background tone, no gutter tone, no distinct diff hue set, and no tool-surface colour that a CodeTracer desktop user would recognise. The result is the explorer register's light palette mapped onto a tool layout: correct density, correct pane vocabulary, but a colour system with only three hues and no roles of its own. Contrast is not the problem here — semantics are.

findings.location: EDITOR pane, shaded lines 30, 33, 35, 36, 38, 39, 41, 45, 47
findings.finding: Lines with no executable step are tinted #ECECEB against the #F3F3F3 line background — a measured 1.065:1, below any perceptual threshold on a display. The state is actually carried by the ~3 px indigo gutter dot on the other lines, so no information is lost, but a surface level has been spent on a signal it cannot deliver, and at closer inspection it reads as arbitrary zebra striping in a code pane rather than as a state.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane — 'Yes' (canonical, y 255–277), 'Safe' (finality, y 286–308), 'Not observable' (y 528–550), 'Trace ready' (y 618–641)
findings.finding: Four badges of identical shape in one pane, with no readable rule for which get colour. 'Trace ready' is green fill on a green border; 'Yes' and 'Safe' — equally affirmative facts — take the same neutral #F3F3F3 fill as 'Not observable', which is the one genuinely negative fact in the group. Grey therefore means both 'confirmed' and 'unavailable' four rows apart.

findings.location: EDITOR gutter, line 32: rail and line number at x 5–48 versus the ▶ arrow at x 76–86, y 452–464; and the timeline fill at x 287–305, y 163–182
findings.finding: The single current-position marker is built from two tints of the same hue: the rail and the line number are #4F46E5, the ▶ arrow two characters away is #6366F1. The timeline's filled bars and the steppable-line gutter dots are also #6366F1 while every other accent on the page is #4F46E5. Two indigos are in use with no rule assigning them.

findings.location: DEBUG CONTROLS pane, unfilled scrubber track x 307–460, y 172
findings.finding: The dotted remainder of the track is #A2A2A2 on white — 2.55:1, under the 3:1 floor for a meaningful graphical object. It is the element that expresses how much of a 1,315-step trace is left, and it renders fainter than every hairline rule on the page.

findings.location: EDITOR pane, right edge x≈683 — lines 26, 40, 41, 42, 43, 48, 49
findings.finding: Seven of the 26 visible source lines are cut off at the pane's right edge mid-token (line 26 ends '…(initial_shield, re', line 41 ends 'after each h', line 42 ends '/ 100;') with no ellipsis, no fade and no visible horizontal scrollbar. Even the pane's own explanatory note is clipped ('…are not in' / 'this window.'). At 680 px the source pane holds roughly 64 monospace columns, which is under the measure this Noir source needs, and nothing on screen tells the reader that content continues.

findings.location: EDITOR pane body, line 26 at y≈320 through line 51 at y≈895
findings.finding: Source line-height is ~23 px for ~14 px monospace (ratio ~1.6) — a reading rhythm, not a tool rhythm. In the register that pays for density this is the most expensive place to spend it: at the desktop app's ~1.4 the same 620 px of pane body would show roughly 33 lines instead of 26, which is seven more lines of context around the pinned position at no legibility cost.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, FEE PAYER value y≈325–370 and TARGET value y≈400–445
findings.finding: Both 40-hex-digit addresses wrap across three right-aligned lines and break mid-byte, leaving a two-character orphan alone on the third line ('32' at y≈370, '4c' at y≈445). A hash that wraps mid-byte cannot be scanned for a prefix/suffix match and cannot be read out or transcribed correctly. The label column beside each also leaves ~40 px of dead space under 'FEE PAYER' and 'TARGET' while the value fights for width, so the ragged wrap is not even buying density.

findings.location: DEBUG CONTROLS band, scrubber at x≈285–455, y≈172
findings.finding: The only graphical expression of position within a 1315-step trace is 170 px wide (~0.13 px per step, with ~28 px filled) inside an 1132 px band. The same row then restates the identical fact twice more — 'Step 128 of 1315 …' occupying ~560 px of prose and '128 / 1315' another ~80 px at the far right. Of three encodings of one number, the one that could show shape (where the current step sits, how the trace is distributed) got the least width and the two redundant textual ones got the most.

findings.location: DEBUG CONTROLS, the eight stepping buttons at x≈18–268, y≈160–186
findings.finding: The controls are icon-only glyphs at ~14 px in light grey on a near-white surface, with three near-identical pairs at this size (the two diagonal step-in/step-out arrows at x≈83–133, the two bracketed single arrows at x≈143–195, the two double arrows at x≈207–265). Both directions are present, so the presence check passes, but at this size and contrast a reader cannot tell which button reverses without hovering, and no keyboard hints are shown anywhere on the band — B10 asks for keyboard affordances to be indicated.

findings.location: Loading banner, y≈62–118, and the stack above the EDITOR pane (y=0 to y≈195)
findings.finding: The banner sets ~15 px prose across only ~590 px in two lines with generous leading, while ~500 px to its right carries only the three phase chips. Set at the pane register's ~13 px the same sentence fits one line. Together the identity bar (62 px), the banner (56 px) and the full-width DEBUG CONTROLS band (~77 px) consume ~195 px — 22% of a 900 px laptop viewport — before the first line of trace content, on the view whose whole claim is density.

findings.location: CALL TRACE pane, y≈455–558 (below the 'Sorted by call order.' footer)
findings.finding: About 105 px of the call-trace pane is empty while the EDITOR beside it is clipping lines horizontally and running content off the bottom edge. The STATE pane below has its own ~40 px of slack at y≈860–893, so no pane is actually starved vertically — but the column split at this viewport leaves visible dead space in the middle column that the source pane could use if the panes shared a horizontal boundary instead of a fixed one.

findings.location: CALL TRACE pane — column header 'ACIR opcodes' at x≈1040–1140, y≈242, and the 'Sort by cost' link at x≈1063, y≈444
findings.finding: One quantity carries two names 200 px apart in the same pane: the numeric column is headed 'ACIR opcodes' but the sort control offers 'cost', so a reader cannot tell whether sorting by cost would reorder by the column they can see or by a measure not shown. The header itself also mixes two treatments in one label — 'ACIR' letterspaced uppercase, 'opcodes' lowercase.

findings.location: STATE pane — 'remaining_shield 9000' at y≈632 versus 'damage 2000' at y≈800
findings.finding: Changed values are marked two different ways with no legend: remaining_shield is accent-coloured text only, damage is accent-coloured text plus an accent bar in the pane's left gutter. If the bar means something distinct (written at this step rather than merely changed) it is unreadable as such; if it means the same thing, the two rows are inconsistently marked. Under load this is the pane where the eye should find the changed values first.

findings.location: EDITOR pane bottom edge, y≈890–900 (line 51)
findings.finding: The editor's last line is cut mid-glyph at the viewport edge and the pane draws no closing bottom border, while the CALL TRACE and STATE panes both close cleanly with a border at y≈893. The left column therefore reads as the page running off the bottom rather than as a bounded scroll container, which undercuts the 'session occupies the viewport' framing at exactly the seam where it is judged.

findings.location: identity bar, back affordance '← aztec' at x≈22–76, y≈31
findings.finding: The only back control in the identity bar is labelled with the chain name, so it reads as 'back to the aztec chain', not 'back to this transaction'. The backbone requires a return path to the transaction detail page, and nothing on the surface names that destination: the truncated hash beside it (x≈93–201) is rendered in plain near-black mono with no link affordance, and the only visible link in the bar area is '101:0' in the TRANSACTION pane, which goes to the block. The crossing out of the product register is supposed to be as visible as the crossing in.

findings.location: EDITOR pane, prose notice at y≈266–300, above line 26
findings.finding: Two lines of explorer-register explanatory copy sit inside the code pane in the UI face — 'Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window.' A desktop editor never narrates its own viewport; it lets the gutter say where the window starts. This is marketing-page voice inside the tool's densest pane, and it costs ~35 px of code at the top of the only pane that is already clipping its content.

findings.location: top banner band, y≈62–118 (prose x≈24–640; three pill chips x≈651–1324)
findings.finding: The phase display is built from explorer primitives: a full-width paragraph plus three 32 px letter-spaced uppercase pills across a 56 px band. The information is right and must stay, but its treatment is a marketing banner. Combined with the 62 px identity bar, ~120 px — 13% of the 900 px viewport — is chrome before the first pane, in a register whose reference application spends that space on a one-line status strip.

findings.location: DEBUG CONTROLS pane, timeline at x≈285–455, y≈166–180
findings.finding: The trace timeline is a ~170 px dotted hairline with a small hatched head, visually subordinate to the 560 px sentence beside it; position is legible only from the text '128 / 1315' at x≈1050. In the CodeTracer desktop app the timeline is a primary, full-width element of the session, not an ornament wedged between the button group and a caption. This is the clearest divergence from the reference application on the screen.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, 'Status reason' at y≈185–207
findings.finding: The value is rendered as the raw internal token 'private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded' — a kebab-case enum member shown as visitor-facing copy, wrapped across two lines in the proportional UI face. Everywhere else on this surface the product speaks English ('no call structure to trace', 'Trace ready'), so this reads as a value that escaped before it was written. Copy is a design property here and this one is machine vocabulary.

findings.location: EDITOR pane right edge (x≈684) versus CALL TRACE pane dead space (y≈455–555)
findings.finding: Source lines 40–49 are cut mid-token at the pane's right edge with no visible horizontal scrollbar or wrap indicator ('fn calculate_shield_regeneration(initial_shield:Field, remaining_shiel'), while the call trace pane holds seven frames and leaves ~100 px blank below 'Sorted by call order.'. The split at 1440 starves the pane whose content is widest and gives slack to the pane that has none to use; a desktop editor either wraps or scrolls, it does not silently truncate code.

findings.location: CALL TRACE pane footer, 'Sort by cost' at x≈1063–1136, y≈444
findings.finding: The sort control is a blue explorer-register text link in the pane's bottom edge, paired with the caption 'Sorted by call order.' Sorting is a pane control and in the reference application lives in the pane header as a toggle or segmented control; as a link at the foot it borrows the web surface's link role and puts a control where a caption is expected.

findings.location: identity bar right cluster, 'NOIR' at x≈1197–1223
findings.finding: An unlabelled grey uppercase datum sits immediately left of the 'Share' and 'Download trace' buttons, at similar size and vertical position, so it reads as a third, disabled button rather than as the VM/language fact it is. Either give it the same badge primitive as 'Partial' or separate it from the control cluster.

findings.location: identity bar hash (x≈93–201) versus TRANSACTION pane hash (y≈162)
findings.finding: The same hash is truncated two different ways on one screen: '0xb63616…6359' (6+4) in the identity bar and '0xb636167a…66d46359' (8+8) in the metadata pane. Hash truncation is a shared primitive across both registers and should have one rule; two rules within 130 px make the two strings momentarily look like two transactions.

findings.location: DEBUG CONTROLS pane, the eight stepping buttons at x 17-269, y 168-195
findings.finding: The stepping toolbar is the control surface for reverse execution, the product's entire premise, and it is the weakest thing on the page. All eight buttons sit at a uniform 2 px gap, so the desktop app's [reverse][forward] pairing is not expressed at all and the row reads as eight unrelated chips; the chips are not a common size (29, 29, 27, 26, 32, 32, 32, 32 px), so the row is visibly ragged; the 7-8 px glyphs measure #818181 on #202020 = 4.18:1, the lowest-contrast interactive element on the screen, while 'Download trace' - a secondary utility in the identity bar - is the brightest control at 15.5:1, inverting the page's control hierarchy. There are no labels, no group separators and no keyboard affordances, and the step-out/continue glyphs (|<-, ->|, |<<, >>|) read as media transport rather than debugger moves, so which chip is reverse-continue cannot be told without hovering.

findings.location: EDITOR pane, source body, lines 26–58 (x≈130–915, y≈310–1070)
findings.finding: The source has no token differentiation whatsoever — `fn`, `let`, `if`, `else`, identifiers, the numeric literals `100`/`0`, the string literal on line 54 and the `//` comment on line 56 are all rendered at one weight in one value (#dddddd on #101010). In the pane the product exists for, a reader gets no structure without reading the words. Weight alone would carry most of it even before colour.

findings.location: CALL TRACE pane header (x≈930, y≈228–240) against its column header row (x≈930, y≈254–266); same relationship in TRANSACTION pane, y≈132 vs y≈231
findings.finding: The pane title and the column header are typographically identical: same mono caps, same ~11px size, same grey, same letterspacing, same left edge, separated only by a hairline. `CALL TRACE` does not out-rank `FRAME`, and `TRANSACTION` does not out-rank `BLOCK` — measured cap heights differ by roughly 1px. Two structural levels are collapsed into one, so the eye cannot tell a pane boundary from a table boundary without reading the words.

findings.location: identity bar hash (x≈95–205, y≈24–40) versus TRANSACTION pane hash (x≈1610–1780, y≈155–172)
findings.finding: The same transaction hash is truncated by two different rules and set in two different typefaces on one screen: `0xb63616…6359` (6 prefix + 4 suffix, monospace, letterforms with squared terminals) in the identity bar, `0xb636167a…66d46359` (8 + 8, geometric UI sans with a single-storey `a` and circular `6`) in the pane. A visitor comparing the two cannot immediately confirm they are the same value, which is the identity bar's only job.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, FEE PAYER value (x≈1637–1910, y≈318–358) and TARGET value (y≈370–408)
findings.finding: Both 42-character addresses are rendered untruncated and soft-wrap to a second right-aligned line, so `e430d5d932` and `a59161624c` sit alone on their own lines with no label beside them and no visual tie to the row above. The wrap point is wherever the container ends, not a chosen boundary — no ellipsis, no middle-truncation, no character-level grouping. This is the widest content in the pane and the only content given no truncation strategy at all, three rows below a hash that does get one.

findings.location: CALL TRACE, current frame row `calculate_damage` (x≈968–1090, y≈400–423), against the identical unselected frame name at y≈330–343
findings.finding: The row you are standing on carries the weakest type in the pane. The unselected `calculate_damage` at y≈336 is bold at #f3f3f3; the current frame's name at y≈411 drops to regular weight and a mid-blue (#818cf8) sitting on the #312e81 selection band — measured 3.8:1, below the 4.5 floor for 13px regular text. Weight and emphasis decrease exactly where hierarchy should peak, so the highlight band is doing all the work and the label is fighting it.

findings.location: EDITOR pane, notice line 'Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below…' (x≈20–762, y≈285–299)
findings.finding: This is UI prose about the pane, but it is set in the same monospace at the same ~13px as the source immediately beneath it, on the same left origin. It reads as line 25 of the file rather than as a message from the tool. B7 names 'code and UI in the same face' as the failing case, and this is the one place in the product where the two abut directly.

findings.location: DEBUG CONTROLS row: 'Step 128 of 1315 — stepping starts when the replay engine finishes loading (18 MB)' (x≈860–1420, y≈173–190) and '128 / 1315' (x≈1435–1520, same baseline)
findings.finding: The position is stated twice on one line, and the hierarchy is inverted between the two. The prose sentence is the brightest text (#f0f0f0, sans, full weight) and carries the numbers proportionally; the tabular monospace readout that a tool user actually scans for is at #919191, the dimmest text in the row. The scannable form should be the emphasised one, and the sentence should not repeat the count it precedes.

findings.location: CALL TRACE opcode column (x≈1460–1520, y≈278–440) versus TRANSACTION 'COST · MANA' value (x≈1690–1910, y≈422–437)
findings.finding: Two numeric treatments for the same class of quantity. The opcode counts are monospace with thousands separators and right-aligned (`1,315`, `1,208`, `96`, `11`); the mana figures a few hundred pixels away are proportional sans with no separators (`88000 / 200000`), so the two five/six-digit numbers cannot be compared by eye and `200000` has to be counted digit by digit. Pick one figure style — tabular, separated — for every quantity in the shell.

findings.location: 'STATE' / 'EVENT LOG' tabs (x≈930–1060, y≈668–685) against the 'DEBUG CONTROLS', 'EDITOR', 'CALL TRACE' and 'TRANSACTION' titles
findings.finding: The pane-title level is expressed two ways. Four panes name themselves with dim grey (#919191) letterspaced caps at ~11px; the state pane names itself with a bold near-white ~12px sans tab plus a blue underline. Same structural role, opposite emphasis — so the state pane's title reads as the loudest header on the screen while the source pane's reads as the quietest.

findings.location: EDITOR pane, source body — baseline pitch measured between lines 26/27/28 (y≈312, 337, 358…)
findings.finding: Line pitch is ≈23px on a ≈13px face, a leading ratio near 1.75 — prose leading in a code pane. CodeTracer's editor sits nearer 1.4, and the difference costs roughly ten lines of context in an 800px-tall pane. Tightening it increases information rather than reducing it.

findings.location: EDITOR pane right edge (x≈915) at line 40 (y≈642) and line 53 (y≈943)
findings.finding: Long source lines are hard-clipped mid-token at the pane edge — `shield_regen_perce` and `damage: Field, r` — with no ellipsis and no static overflow affordance visible at rest. Horizontal scroll inside the code container is the right behaviour, but this is a fourth truncation appearance on a screen that already has three, and nothing marks the cut.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, 'Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded' (x≈1540–1900, y≈182–212)
findings.finding: A machine enum value is set as proportional running prose and wraps at its own hyphen (`public-part-` / `succeeded`), which reads as a hyphenated English word break rather than as one indivisible token. Identifiers of this kind belong in the mono face, or in the same pill treatment used for `Partial` and `Trace ready`.

findings.location: STATE pane, `masses[2]` row (x≈940, y≈800–816) under its parent `masses` (y≈775–791)
findings.finding: The only cue that this row is a child of the array above it is a single monospace-character indent (~8px). At one level of nesting it is already ambiguous with a slightly longer name; there is no guide, no rule and no weight change to express the relationship.

findings.location: CALL TRACE column header, 'ACIR opcodes' (x≈1425–1520, y≈254–266)
findings.finding: This header mixes an all-caps token with a lowercase word in one label, and drops the second word to a dimmer value, while every other header on the screen ('FRAME', 'STATE', 'BLOCK', 'CANONICAL') is uniform caps. It reads as two labels rather than one, and breaks the caps-header convention at the only place it carries a unit.

findings.location: Call trace pane, selected frame row (x 929–1520, y 403–420)
findings.finding: The current frame's name renders #818cf8 on the #312e81 selection fill at 3.83:1 and its path 'zk_shields · src/shield.nr' at 3.62:1 — both below the 4.5:1 floor at ~12px, and the lowest-contrast text anywhere on the page. resolutions.evidence: client/src/pages/tx.nim: the H1 called truncHash(v.hash, lead=10, tail=8) while the breadcrumb called truncHash(v.hash) with its 6/4 defaults, so ONE hash appeared at three lengths inside 130 vertical pixels. The H1 now uses the same defaults, so the page has exactly two forms — one truncation rule and the full value. MEASURED on the rebuilt page: the distinct 0x-prefixed string lengths are 11 (truncated), 42 (full), 10 (the selector) and 2 ('0x'), i.e. one truncation length, not three.

client/src/components/styles.nim adds `.badge.lg` at --bt-type-body-sm-size with --bt-space-2xs/--bt-space-sm padding, and client/src/pages/tx.nim renders the hero outcome with it. The hero status badge moves from the 12px label rung to the 14px body rung beside the 32px H1, so the second most important fact on a page about reverted transactions is no longer the smallest type in the hero.

client/src/pages/tx.nim: the cost cell was `c.used & " / " & c.limit & " " & c.unit` in one .identifier span with no space before the token parenthetical. The figures keep the identifier treatment; the unit and the token drop to .muted, and the space is restored — `42000 / 100000` mono, then ` mana (FeeJuice)` at the secondary level. The digits are the scannable part again. Thousands grouping is NOT addressed: the values arrive as strings from the data contract and inserting separators would be the view computing a presentation of a chain-native quantity, which Data-Contract.md forbids the view from doing. Left for VD.4 with the fee rows.

client/src/components/styles.nim: `.sec-title` margin-bottom moved from --bt-rhythm-stack (24px) to --bt-space-xs (8px) while `.sec-title.next` keeps padding-top: --bt-rhythm-stack (24px) below its rule. MEASURED on the rebuilt page, gap above / gap below for the six headings: 100/8, 100/8, 100/24, 48/24, 48/24, 100/8. Every heading is now 3x-4x closer to the content it labels than to the boundary above it, so proximity binds each heading downwards.

client/src/components/styles.nim adds `.sec-title.sibling` at --bt-rhythm-group (48px) with no rule, and client/src/pages/tx.nim applies it to Internal calls and State changes — three one-sentence sibling sections are separated by the GROUP step and the group as a whole by the SECTION step, which is what the four rhythm roles exist to express. MEASURED: the section gaps are now 100/100/100/48/48/100px rather than six identical 100px aprons, and the page is 2583px tall against 2785px before.

client/src/components/styles.nim: `.debugcard .note.spec` gains max-width:none. The rule was asymmetric (25px left, 65px right) because it belonged to a paragraph capped at --bt-measure-prose sitting inside a card capped at --bt-layout-prose — two different measures, one nested in the other. The rule now spans the card's content box, and the card's own width is the measure.

client/src/components/styles.nim: every container now carries the SAME hairline in --bt-border-default — the trace card (was --bt-border-strong, read as borderless beside its overlay shadow), the code block (was --bt-border-subtle plus a fill) and the callouts (which also lose their thick left spine). Containers are ranked by ONE axis, elevation: the trace card is the only panel carrying --bt-elevation-overlay, the data panels carry --bt-elevation-raised, the callouts carry none. One idiom, one ranking.

client/src/pages/tx.nim renders Canonical with the neutral badge role instead of the success role — canonicality is a registry fact, not an execution outcome — so green means execution status and only that. client/src/viewutil.nim returns the information role for taOnDemand, so the trace-coverage state the page turns on carries a hue again. The two axes stay distinguishable by SHAPE as well as colour: a status badge is a filled rectangle, a coverage chip is an outlined pill with a leading dot (.badge.coverage).

The four emphasis levels were not the problem — the ROLE ASSIGNMENT was: --bt-text-muted (#484848) carried breadcrumb, eyebrow, grid labels, every explanatory panel and the footer at once. client/src/components/styles.nim spreads them: chrome (breadcrumb, eyebrow, footer) drops to --bt-text-subtle, labels stay --bt-text-muted, and explanatory PROSE — which is content, not chrome — rises to --bt-text-default. Three levels now do three jobs. Widening the ladder further is not available in pure greys: on the sunken surface (#f3f3f3) only neutral.450 and darker clear 4.5:1, which is why the rungs are close; VD.10 owns the palette audit.

client/src/components/styles.nim: the section rules move from --bt-border-subtle (#c8c8c8, 1.86:1 on white) to --bt-border-default (#a2a2a2, 2.60:1). It is an improvement, not conformance: WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor applies to UI components and meaningful graphics, and a decorative section rule is neither — the section boundary is also carried by a 100px gap and a heading. A 3:1 rule grid would read as a spreadsheet in a marketing-grade register. Recorded here rather than exempted; VD.10 re-runs the audit over the final palette.

Same change as tx-detail/wide/light/L2/5, which L4 reached independently from the density lens: `.sec-title.sibling` at --bt-rhythm-group for the three trace-derived sections. Two reviewers with different lenses measured the same defect, which is the signal the five-lens design exists to produce.

resolutions.reason: P3. The two widths are a decision, not raggedness: data panels take the column (--bt-layout-container), prose panels take one shared prose width (--bt-layout-prose). This is a recorded TENSION rather than an agreement — L2 asked twice for the trace panel to be narrowed to its content (round 3) and then for one right edge (round 5), and those cannot both hold. The narrowing won because a 910px box around a 150px button and two sentences made the container outweigh the control it holds. What WAS fixed is the accidental part: the two prose panels previously sat at different widths because --bt-measure-prose is in `ch` and they were set at different font sizes; both now use one px token, so the page has two widths rather than three.

P3. The 92px vs 100px difference is margin collapsing between the trace card's box and the following section's margin-top, not a second spacing step: both are --bt-rhythm-section. Correcting it would mean giving one boundary a hand-written offset, which is the class of ad-hoc margin the rhythm roles exist to eliminate. Read and declined.
